findings.claim: "He instructs the group to find a man - any man - and plant Adam's DNA on him... Phil's plan requires the group to steal Adam's jumper (which has his DNA on it) and leave it near this stranger." Repeated in the key fact, the takeaway, knowledge check 1 ("Planting Adam's DNA on an innocent man to frame him"), flashcard 10, lesson 1 ("Cathy... volunteers to threaten the postman") and lesson 5.
findings.truth: The mechanism is the other way round. Brian gives the police a false description of a man in the woods. Cathy then finds a postman who matches it and gets him to handle Adam's jumper, so the INNOCENT MAN'S DNA is on it. The police find the jumper, arrest him, and Brian identifies him. Cathy never threatens him.
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/summary - "Cathy purposefully found a fat postman who fit Phil's made-up description and got him to handle the sweater"; https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/character-list - Cathy "Frames an innocent postman by having him handle Adam's jumper"; https://www.litcharts.com/lit/dna/summary - "Cathy obtains DNA evidence by locating a man fitting that description at a local post office... Phil coerces Brian into identifying the innocent man".

findings.claim: Phil's instructions quoted as "Take his jumper. Leave it there. Go home. Say nothing." - given in lesson 2 (content + key fact + flashcard), lesson 5 (key fact + flashcard) and lesson 7 (content + key fact + flashcard + the euphemism paragraph).
findings.truth: No such line exists. It is a fabricated quotation, and it also encodes the inverted DNA mechanism of F1. Phil's plan speech in the first section is long and circumstantial ("Cathy and Mark you meet them there, but on the way you find a quiet street..."). The lessons now describe his flat, unexplained instructions instead of quoting an invented line.
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/quotes - Phil, Scene One p.21; no such line in any quotation list for the play.

findings.claim: Phil "orders the group to keep Adam hidden - to take him to a disused building"; lesson 4 says "Adam is presumably still hidden"; lesson 5 says Phil "orchestrates Adam's imprisonment" and Adam is "imprisoned when found alive". Adam's death is never mentioned anywhere in the unit.
findings.truth: At the end of the third section Phil orders Adam killed - taken back to the woods with a bag over his head - and Brian and Cathy carry it out offstage. Phil's argument is that everyone already thinks Adam is dead, so it changes nothing. There is no disused building and no imprisonment. A student taught this unit would get the ending of the play wrong.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/dna/summary - "Phil then instructs the medicated Brian to kill Adam using a plastic bag"; https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/summary - "manipulate him into suffocating Adam with a bag offstage. Cathy supervised this killing"; https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/character-list - Adam "Eventually killed via suffocation".

findings.claim: "The boy the group assumed was dead... is found by Cathy."
findings.truth: Brian finds Adam alive in the wood; Mark and Jan bring the news to Leah and Phil in the field.
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/character-list - Brian "discovers Adam alive in the forest"; https://www.litcharts.com/lit/dna/summary - "Mark and Jan arrive with shocking news: Adam has been discovered alive in the woods".

findings.claim: A "Cigarette Scene": Cathy tortures Adam by burning him with a lit cigarette, described as "the play's most violent moment" and "one of the few violent acts staged onstage". Carried by the collapsible heading, the takeaway, knowledge check 2, the matching question, two flashcards, two mark schemes, and repeated in lessons 4 and 5.
findings.truth: There is no such scene. Cathy does not torture Adam. Cigarette burns belong to the ORIGINAL bullying of Adam, reported by Mark in the first section. Kelly stages no violence at all; Adam's killing happens offstage.
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/summary - the bullying account: "They made him eat leaves, endure hitting, and suffer cigarette burns"; neither the LitCharts nor the GradeSaver account of the third section contains any cigarette torture.

findings.claim: "Richard starts to question Phil openly: 'Happy? Is that what you are? Happy?'" - carried by the key fact, the exam tip, practice question 5, knowledge check 3, the matching question and two flashcards, plus lesson 5 and a lesson 8 mark scheme.
findings.truth: The "happy" challenge is Leah's, not Richard's. Phil justifies himself by saying everyone is happier; Leah is the one who asks what the word even means. The unit contradicts itself - lesson 7 correctly gives the line to Leah.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/dna/quotes - Leah, Scene 2: "What is happy, what's happy all about, who says you're supposed to be happy"; https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/quotes - Phil, Scene Three p.54: "I'm in charge. Everyone is happier."

findings.claim: "DNA was first performed at the National Theatre in 2008 as part of the NT Connections programme" - repeated in the key fact, the takeaway, knowledge check 1 (options offered no 2007), two flashcards and the lesson 8 context list ("the 2008 premiere").
findings.truth: Kelly wrote DNA for the 2007 National Theatre Connections festival and it was first performed that year by young casts. The National Theatre's own production (Cottesloe) followed in 2008. The knowledge check had no correct option, so option 2 is changed to 2007.
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Kelly - "For the 2007 National Theatre Connections Festival, he wrote DeoxyriboNucleic Acid (better known by the title DNA) which after the connections received a professional production".

findings.claim: "making him steal vodka, setting his socks on fire, putting a plastic bag over his head... They took Adam to a grille in the woods and dared him to walk across it. He fell." Repeated in the key fact, whose revision tip asks for the four acts in order.
findings.truth: The reported bullying is: made him eat leaves, hit him, burned him with cigarettes and made him steal vodka. The plastic bag belongs to Adam's killing, not the bullying. Adam does not simply fall: the group throw stones at him while he crosses the grille and one hits him.
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/summary - "They made him eat leaves, endure hitting, and suffer cigarette burns. While drunk on stolen vodka, they threw stones at Adam as he crossed a metal grille over a shaft. One stone struck his head and he fell."; https://www.litcharts.com/lit/dna/quotes - Mark, Scene One p.18: "And someone's pegged a stone at him...".

findings.claim: "Mark and Jan report that she has taken charge of the group" and "Mark and Jan reveal the fates of other group members."
findings.truth: Richard reports the group's fates to a silent Phil in the final field scene (John Tate's religion, Brian's medication, Danny and the dentist's, Cathy's gang). Mark and Jan only open the section with the news that Leah has gone.
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/summary - "Richard describes the group's deteriorated states..."; https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/character-list - Richard "later visits the isolated Phil".

findings.claim: "an ice cream in Act 1, a muffin in Act 2, chips in Act 3".
findings.truth: The study guides record Phil eating a waffle in the third section, not chips.
findings.evidence: https://www.litcharts.com/lit/dna/quotes - quote entry headed "Phil's Waffle Moment (Scene 3), p.45-46".

findings.claim: A script extract quoted as the play's dialogue: "MARK: So we were - / JAN: Having a laugh. / MARK: Having a laugh, we were, and - / JAN: He fell."
findings.truth: That exchange is invented. Replaced with the play's real opening exchange between Jan and Mark, which makes the same point about clipped, shared dialogue.
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/quotes - Scene One p.2, JAN and MARK: "DEAD?" / "Yeah." / "What, dead?" / "Yeah." / "Like dead, dead?" / "Yes."

findings.claim: John Tate bans the word dead: "I'm in charge and no one, I'm telling you, no one is going to use that word." Lesson 5 gives a shorter variant, and the lesson 2 mark scheme quotes "no one is going to use that word".
findings.truth: The printed line is "Alright. New rule; that word is banned." A student quoting the invented version would lose the AO2 credit that a precise quotation earns.
findings.evidence: https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/quotes - John Tate, Scene One p.8; https://www.litcharts.com/lit/dna/quotes - John Tate, same wording (p.13 in that edition).

findings.claim: "It tells us everything we need to know about Phil's character in seven words."
findings.truth: "Phil is eating an ice cream" is six words. Also corrected in the practice question that repeats the claim.

findings.claim: Lesson titles and body text call the play's divisions "Acts" ("Acts 1-2", "Act 3", "Act 4").
findings.truth: The published text has four sections headed One, Two, Three and Four, each cycling A Street / A Field / A Wood. The usage is consistent across the unit, so it is recorded rather than rewritten; titles are not editable through the edits file.
findings.evidence: published Oberon text structure; https://www.litcharts.com/lit/dna/summary uses Part One-Four.

findings.claim: Quotations that no available source corroborates and that the in-copyright text was needed to settle: "Phil is eating an ice cream" (lessons 2, 5, 6, plus two knowledge checks and two flashcards), Leah's "We share 99.6% of our DNA with them" and "But we choose chimps" (lessons 2, 5, 7 and a knowledge check), "You need me, Phil. Everyone needs someone.", Phil's "I'm not saying anything" (lesson 7 heading, a knowledge check and a practice question), "Are you happy? Is that what you are?", "We've found a man", and Leah threatening to set fire to herself (lessons 2 and 5).
findings.truth: Two options. (1) Leave them: they are plausible and no source contradicts them, and "I'm not saying anything" carries a whole lesson 7 section. (2) Check all seven against the printed Oberon edition in one pass and correct together - the recommended route, because this unit has already produced four fabricated quotations. I have edited only the quotations I could disprove. ORCHESTRATOR: unverifiable without the printed text; left as NOTE for a check against the Oberon edition.
findings.evidence: not found in https://www.litcharts.com/lit/dna/quotes , https://www.gradesaver.com/dna/study-guide/quotes , https://www.litcharts.com/lit/dna/summary ; WebSearch budget exhausted for this session.

findings.claim: "an unseen extract from another modern drama or prose text".
findings.truth: The unseen extract in part (a) is same-genre, so a drama set text is paired with a modern play.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md, forms of assessment: "A comparison of an extract from the studied text with a modern, same-genre unseen extract".

findings.claim: Exam framing across the unit: closed text component, Section A modern prose or drama, one compulsory question in two parts, (a) comparison with an unseen extract 20 marks and (b) a related question on the same text 20 marks, no SPaG.
findings.truth: Correct. No lesson claims a paper number, a choice of two questions, a 30+4 or 40-mark essay, an AO split, or SPaG marks. All 48 practice questions are labelled 20 marks, which matches the real question.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md sections 3a and 3h (AO4 assessed in Section B of each component only).

findings.claim: Every practice ladder in the unit (48 questions across all 8 lessons) names two different mark ranges "Top band" (17-20 and 13-16) and ends with "Lower band (1-4)", which is not a house band name.
findings.truth: The mark ranges are right for a 20-mark question. Relabelled to the five house bands: Top band (17-20), Upper-mid band (13-16), Mid band (9-12), Lower-mid band (5-8), Low band (1-4).

summary: The exam layer is clean, but the plot layer is not: the unit inverts the DNA-planting mechanism, never mentions that Adam is killed, invents a Cathy cigarette-torture scene, gives Leah's "Happy?" challenge to Richard, misattributes the discovery of Adam, and quotes four lines that are not in the play. 126 edits across all 8 lessons; the premiere year and the bullying account are also corrected.
